body:
## Summary

The `v` index level is supposed to identify a sampling cluster. For some
countries it is **wave-scoped**: the same enumeration area carries a different
`v` in each round, with no crosswalk and no warning. A caller who groups or
joins on `v` across waves silently splits one cluster into several.

Found while building a two-wave GLSS panel for a workshop: every panel reshape
needs a `.droplevel('v')` first, which is what prompted the check.

## Evidence

Measured on `lsms_library` 0.14.0, GhanaLSS GLSS1/GLSS2, over the 712
households the household crosswalk links across `1987-88` and `1988-89`:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| households keeping the same `v` | **0 of 712** |
| first character of `v`, 1987-88 | always `1` |
| first character of `v`, 1988-89 | always `2` |
| match after stripping the first character | 2 of 712 |
| distinct `(v87, v88)` cluster pairs | 79 |
| a `v87` mapping to more than one `v88` | 0 |
| a `v88` mapping to more than one `v87` | 0 |
| paired clusters agreeing on `Region` | **79 of 79** |
| paired clusters agreeing on `Rural` | **79 of 79** |

So it is not a prefix and it is not noise. It is a clean **bijection between 79
GLSS1 clusters and 79 GLSS2 clusters**, and the paired clusters are the same
places: `1003 -> 2009`, both `Western`/`Rural`; `1013 -> 2049`, both
`Greater Accra`/`Rural`. Every household in 1003 moves to 2009 together.

This is faithful passthrough, not an invention: `GhanaLSS/1987-88/_/data_info.yml`
maps `v: CLUST`, and GLSS renumbered its clusters between rounds. The defect is
that a wave-scoped code is served on an index level whose purpose is to identify
a cluster, with nothing to say so.

## It is not consistent across the corpus

Households observed in three consecutive waves, share keeping the same `v`:

| country | waves | households | same `v` throughout |
|---|---|---|---|
| GhanaLSS | 1987-88, 1988-89 (2 waves) | 712 | **0 (0%)** |
| Uganda | 2009-10, 2010-11, 2011-12 | 2,440 | **0 (0%)** |
| Tanzania | 2008-09, 2010-11, 2012-13 | 2,895 | 2,305 (80%) |

Tanzania is the interesting row: `v` *is* stable there for most panel
households, so the intended semantics appears to be that a household which does
not move keeps its cluster. Ghana and Uganda do not honour that, and a caller
has no way to tell which regime a country is in.

(GhanaLSS also carries a literal `Mover` sentinel in `v`, so movers are modelled
explicitly there -- which makes the wholesale renumbering harder to read as
intentional.)

## Why it matters beyond ergonomics

1. **Inference.** `v` is the natural level to cluster standard errors on. In a
   panel, clustering on `v` as served treats one EA observed twice as two
   independent clusters, overstating the number of clusters and understating
   standard errors. Nothing warns you.
2. **Silent joins.** `groupby('v')`, or a merge of cluster-level covariates onto
   a panel, splits each EA per wave and produces plausible-looking wrong answers.
3. **Reshapes.** Any `unstack('t')` on a table carrying `v` needs `droplevel('v')`
   first or it yields one row per household-wave rather than per household.

## Reproduction

```python
import lsms_library as ll, pandas as pd
g  = ll.Country("GhanaLSS")
hc = g.household_characteristics(waves=["1987-88", "1988-89"])
idx  = hc.index.to_frame(index=False)[["t", "v", "i"]].drop_duplicates()
wide = idx.pivot_table(index="i", columns="t", values="v", aggfunc="first").dropna()
print(len(wide), (wide["1987-88"].astype(str) == wide["1988-89"].astype(str)).sum())
# 712 0

pairs = wide.drop_duplicates()
print(len(pairs), pairs.groupby("1987-88")["1988-89"].nunique().gt(1).sum())
# 79 0   -- a bijection

cf = g.cluster_features(waves=["1987-88", "1988-89"]).reset_index()
# Region and Rural agree for all 79 pairs
```

## Possible resolutions

Not a request for a particular one:

- A **cluster crosswalk** analogous to `panel_ids`, giving a stable cluster
  identity across waves. For GLSS1/GLSS2 it is recoverable exactly as above --
  the household crosswalk already determines the 79 pairs -- so it need not be
  hand-built.
- Failing that, **declare the regime**: something in `data_scheme` saying whether
  a country's `v` is wave-scoped or panel-stable, and warn on a cross-wave
  `groupby`/join when it is wave-scoped. The `null_read_audit` / `quantity_audit`
  machinery is the obvious model.
- At minimum, **document it**, so that `droplevel('v')` is a known step rather
  than something each caller rediscovers.

Checked GhanaLSS, Uganda, Tanzania and Malawi only; the other declared panel
countries are unexamined.

comments.body:
Diagnosis and design done; **no crosswalk built, and the recommendation is not to build one under this issue.** Full note committed at `slurm_logs/2026-09-18_gh942_cluster_identity/DESIGN.org` (with the measurement scripts beside it). Headlines, because several of them change this issue's premises.

## The blocking contradiction is settled

`GhanaLSS/_/CONTENTS.org:390` calls GLSS2 a "fresh draw"; this issue measures a clean 79↔79 bijection with GLSS1. **GLSS2 is not a fresh draw** — it is a half-retained rotating panel. GSS's own `G3report.pdf` (Appendix 1, printed p.110), already quoted at `CONTENTS.org:927`, says half of GLSS1's workloads were retained for GLSS2 and the other half drawn from master-sample replicate 6. The warm cache realises exactly that: 176 and 170 clusters, 79 paired, 97 and 91 unpaired. `CONTENTS.org:1109` already flags the table as wrong and records the tension as **unresolved**.

Two caveats for anyone deriving a crosswalk: the 79 is a **lower bound** (half of 176 is ~88, so either nine retained workloads yielded no re-interview or "workload" ≠ "EA"), and it is **complete for what it can be** — the unpaired clusters are genuinely different EAs, not missing linkage.

## Two instances this issue did not have

- **Ethiopia 2011-12 → 2013-14 is a cleaner case than GhanaLSS**: `ea_id` → `ea_id2`, disjoint code spaces, 3,776 panel households, 0% agreement, and a **complete 333→433 bijection with zero violations**. The survey itself calls `ea_id2` a re-identification. And the ESS may ship the crosswalk directly — `CONTENTS.org:978` lists `Pub_ETH_HouseholdGeovars_Y2` as carrying both id generations. Unverified; it is the one bounded check to run before writing any derivation code.
- **CotedIvoire's CILSS (1985-89) is a same-era rotating half-panel that KEPT its cluster numbers** — 100 PSUs, `nA = nB = 100` every year, zero violations. So GLSS's renumbering is a choice GSS made, not a property of 1980s LSMS rotation.

## Three corrections

1. **Tanzania.** The 0% cell is the **extended panel** at 2014-15 → 2019-20 (849 tracked households, 310 pairs, **131 non-bijective** — a crosswalk is not recoverable there even in principle). The 2019-20 → 2020-21 refresh has *zero* shared households and therefore says nothing about `v` at all. Two different boundaries, two different facts.
2. **The `Mover` sentinel is not reproduced.** It occurs zero times in GhanaLSS `sample`/`cluster_features`, and `grep -rn Mover lsms_library/countries/` returns nothing. It is `transformations.py:507`, a library-wide default for a NaN `v`, applied to every country. The reading that it makes GLSS renumbering "harder to read as intentional" does not stand — the sentinel is ours.
3. **Uganda is three defects and only the third is this issue**, so it must not be folded in: (a) two *renderings* of the same `comm` variable — 272 of 322 pairs differ by one digit inserted at position 3, 50 are genuine district recodes, so the 0% at two boundaries is **ours, not GSS's**; (b) `coalesce_coord_bin` making **339 of 656** 2009-10 "clusters" 0.05° GPS bins; (c) a genuine EA → parish → name-composite meaning change, which admits no crosswalk.

## Method caveat worth carrying

Household-`i` overlap lies two ways: countries whose `i` restarts 1..N each wave manufacture spurious linkage (Tajikistan, Panama — neither has any `panel_ids` config, and the WB documentation says outright they are not panels), and countries whose `i` embeds `v` cannot show a mover. **Only five countries yield independent evidence**: GhanaLSS, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Tanzania, Uganda.

## Design, in one line each

Declare per **wave boundary**, not per country (a single tag is wrong for all five informative countries). **Two orthogonal fields** — `household_continuity` and `cluster_id_continuity` — because refresh-by-design is a household fact and renumbering is a cluster fact, and Tanzania is both at different boundaries; the one-dimensional enum in "Possible resolutions" cannot express that. Put it in the `panel:` block of a `sampling.yml` sibling (#793), landing only that block now so #942 does not wait on #793's full curation. Placement cost measured off `country.py:706, 921, 3546, 3558`: a new `.yml` sibling moves **no** hash; a block inside `data_scheme.yml` invalidates **every** L2-country parquet of that country.

**Warn at `Country`, not at `Feature`** — this issue's own reproduction is a single-country two-wave call, so copying the population precedent's placement would put the warning exactly where the bug is not. Nothing served changes under any setting except an opt-in `LSMS_CLUSTER_STRICT=1`.

**The crosswalk is out of scope**: it is derivable at exactly two boundaries in the whole corpus (GhanaLSS 1987-88→1988-89 as a floor, Ethiopia 2011-12→2013-14 complete), and a crosswalk built on this issue's method would be read as covering a class it does not cover.

Seven decisions are stated as questions at the end of the note, with options and consequences — including whether Uganda's rendering defect becomes its own issue and whether `CONTENTS.org:390` is corrected here or separately.

title: v is wave-scoped in some countries: the same cluster gets a new id each round, with no crosswalk
